entries.animalRule: No light of any kind, and the room must be cleared of trip hazards first.
entries.userBenefit: A short sharp burst that shows how quickly your eyes actually adapt.
entries.mechanismConnection: Swordfish — Heated Eyes in Cold Water — Descending • Resolving • Slashing: A block of muscle behind the eye has stopped contracting and become a heater, holding the eyes and brain far above the surrounding water so that vision stays fast enough to track prey during dives into cold dark layers This Trial translates that heater organ keeping vision working in the cold dark into a target found and taken without light.

entries.title: Grind Down the Pile
entries.objective: Create a large visible change through nonstop small repetitions.
entries.animalRule: Transform the pile through repeated small actions; move only one item per action.
entries.userBenefit: Shows how relentless small repetitions can create a large visible result under pressure.
entries.mechanismConnection: Blue Parrotfish repeatedly scrape and grind tiny amounts of reef material, cumulatively producing large quantities of sand. This HIGH Trial compresses that cumulative mechanism into five intense minutes of one-at-a-time processing.

entries.title: Grip One Pencil Without Moving Feet
entries.objective: Complete one pencil while feet stay planted as a one-off expression of Tail-Curl Mooring.
entries.animalRule: Complete exactly one uninterrupted attempt; do not switch activities until one pencil while feet stay planted is complete.
entries.userBenefit: You turn tail-curl mooring into a concrete one-off experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Seahorse — Gripping a stem • Eyes moving separately • Snapping the head upward: Wraps a square-sectioned prehensile tail around seagrass so the body stays fixed against current, then takes tiny crustaceans by rotating the head upward in a few thousandths of a second with a snout shaped to make almost no bow wave ahead of it This Trial translates that mid mechanism into one safe human action: Grip One Pencil Without Moving Feet.

entries.title: Guard One Object Without Touching It
entries.objective: Complete one object without touching as a one-off expression of Cold Century.
entries.animalRule: Use one calm attempt only; remain with the same setup until one object without touching is complete.
entries.userBenefit: You turn cold century into a concrete one-off experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Greenland Shark — Swimming at under a metre a second in near-freezing water • Growing about a centimetre a year • Not breeding until past a century old: Runs its entire physiology at the rate permanent cold allows, with metabolism, growth, swimming speed and maturation all depressed together, which produces a lifespan measured in centuries and a first reproduction later than most vertebrates live This Trial translates that low mechanism into one safe human action: Guard One Object Without Touching It.

entries.title: Have a Picnic Somewhere Scenic
entries.objective: Eat one simple meal outdoors at a place chosen for the view.
entries.animalRule: Slow the experience down: hold one location for the whole meal rather than eating while moving.
entries.userBenefit: Turns a slow held location into a memorable meal rather than a pass-through stop.
entries.mechanismConnection: Pygmy Three-toed Sloth expresses Island Slowness through this mode: Runs a reduced body on red mangrove leaves within a single strip of coastal forest, so the whole energy budget shrinks with the island. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action. This Trial translates that low mechanism into one safe, one-off human action: Have a Picnic Somewhere Scenic.

entries.title: Hide One Eyesore in Plain Sight
entries.objective: Use an outer layer to make one ugly everyday object disappear into the room.
entries.animalRule: Change only the removable outer layer.
entries.userBenefit: You improve your space and practise visual camouflage through design.
entries.mechanismConnection: Citrus Mealybug — Settled • Wax-covered • Sap-fed: A powdery wax layer is secreted over the body while the insect stays put and drinks phloem. Citrus Mealybugs produce a waxy, white coating that helps them blend into the surfaces of citrus trees, making them less visible to predators. This Trial translates that mechanism into use an outer layer to make one ugly everyday object disappear into the room.

entries.title: Hide One Object Among Vertical Lines
entries.objective: Use broken outlines instead of simple colour matching.
entries.animalRule: Keep the object uncovered; only surrounding vertical lines may break its outline.
entries.userBenefit: You learn how shape disruption can hide something even when its colour is not a perfect match.
entries.mechanismConnection: European Perch — Carries bold vertical bars that break the body outline against the vertical lines of reeds, roots and branches, which lets a mid-sized ambush predator hold position inside structure where an unmarked fish would be conspicuous. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Hide One Shape Inside a Matching Line
entries.objective: Hide One Shape Inside a Matching Line.
entries.animalRule: It must be photographed from normal distance, with only its position changed.
entries.userBenefit: You get a concrete, memorable result while practising tail regeneration as a real human action.
entries.mechanismConnection: Southeastern Five-lined Skink — Advertises the tail with a colour brighter than anything else on the body so that a predator strikes there, then detaches it at a preformed fracture plane in the vertebrae, where muscle and blood vessels are arranged to seal and the shed tail writhes for minutes The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Hide Then Jump Back Into View
entries.objective: Use stillness and transparency-like concealment before one explosive exit.
entries.animalRule: Stay still for five seconds, then exit sideways in one fast movement.
entries.userBenefit: You create a genuinely surprising reveal by contrasting near-invisibility with sudden movement.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Prawn — Carries a cuticle and tissues transparent enough that light passes through rather than reflecting, so the outline effectively disappears in open water, with only the eyes and gut remaining visible as the residual giveaway. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Hide Three Sticks in Vertical Lines
entries.objective: Hide Three Sticks in Vertical Lines.
entries.animalRule: All three must sit vertically among matching lines; one leaning object ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: You create a simple camouflage illusion by matching orientation rather than colour.
entries.mechanismConnection: Swims permanently head down with the body vertical, which matches the line of the sea urchin spines it shelters among and makes a group of fish read as more spines, so the concealment depends on posture rather than on colour or shape

entries.title: Hide Three Tokens in Separate Spots
entries.objective: Complete three tokens in separate spots as a one-off expression of Cache Agility.
entries.animalRule: Complete exactly one uninterrupted attempt; do not switch activities until three tokens in separate spots is complete.
entries.userBenefit: You turn cache agility into a concrete one-off experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Eastern Gray Squirrel — Burying one nut per hole • Faking caches when watched • Recovering by memory and smell: Spreads thousands of separate single-item caches across a territory rather than building one store, relocating them later by spatial memory backed by scent, and performing deceptive burials without a nut when another squirrel is watching This Trial translates that mid mechanism into one safe human action: Hide Three Tokens in Separate Spots.

entries.title: Hijack Your Own Conversation
entries.objective: Practise making a sudden bold switch and recovering smoothly.
entries.animalRule: The burst must be sudden, brief, unmistakable, and followed by an immediate return to normal.
entries.userBenefit: You practise social boldness, rapid switching, and recovering composure after doing something deliberately ridiculous.
entries.mechanismConnection: Cetti's Warbler — Explosive • Loud • Brief: A sudden very loud song burst delivered from inside cover, then silence again. Cetti's Warblers are secretive wetland birds that are often heard before they are seen, using loud explosive song from dense cover. This Trial translates that mechanism into practise making a sudden bold switch and recovering smoothly.

entries.title: Hit Five Targets in Silence
entries.objective: Turn one burst of action into a quiet precision run.
entries.animalRule: One hit is required on each of the five targets.
entries.userBenefit: You train focus, precision, and composure while creating an obvious scoreable challenge.
entries.mechanismConnection: Spotted Wood Owl — Drop • Silent • Decisive: A brief muffled descent onto a target whose position was fixed before launch. Spotted Wood Owls hunt at night using large eyes, sensitive hearing, soft flight feathers, and strong talons to approach prey through dark wooded habitats. This Trial translates that mechanism into turn one burst of action into a quiet precision run.

entries.title: Hold One Breathless Rest Without Exercise
entries.objective: Complete quietly without exertion as a one-off expression of Basking Balance.
entries.animalRule: Use one calm attempt only; remain with the same setup until quietly without exertion is complete.
entries.userBenefit: You turn basking balance into a concrete one-off experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Painted Turtle — Under the ice • No oxygen at all • Dissolving its own shell to survive it: Passes months sealed beneath ice with no access to air, abandoning oxygen metabolism entirely and neutralising the lactic acid that accumulates by releasing carbonate from its shell and skeleton into the blood This Trial translates that low mechanism into one safe human action: Hold One Breathless Rest Without Exercise.

entries.title: Hold One Flat Object in Airflow
entries.objective: Use a broad surface as a working fin against moving air.
entries.animalRule: Use gentle airflow only; the sheet must remain under control.
entries.userBenefit: You turn a large surface into a steering tool and feel how orientation changes force.
entries.mechanismConnection: Grayling — Carries a dorsal fin far larger than any other salmonid's and uses it as a working surface in current, bracing against the flow to hold position and turning on it, as well as spreading it in territorial and courtship display. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Hold One Grip Without Readjusting
entries.objective: Stay attached to one safe hold without constantly resetting.
entries.animalRule: Use one comfortable grip only; no readjusting during the minute.
entries.userBenefit: You practise patient sustained control instead of solving discomfort with constant movement.
entries.mechanismConnection: Medicinal Leech — Injects a saliva containing a direct thrombin inhibitor, a vasodilator and an anaesthetic while cutting, which keeps the wound open and painless long enough to take several times the animal's own body weight in one feed that then lasts for months. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Hold One Sticky Problem for Fifteen
entries.objective: Stay with a stubborn problem instead of abandoning it.
entries.animalRule: Do not switch to another task during the fifteen minutes.
entries.userBenefit: You practise patient persistence and make real progress on something that normally makes you escape.
entries.mechanismConnection: Red Assassin Bug — Creeping • Adhesive • Warned: Pads of dense fine hairs on the forelegs grip a struggling caterpillar while bold orange marking warns anything watching that the bug is not worth eating. Milkweed Assassin Bugs are predatory insects that use sticky forelegs and piercing mouthparts to seize prey from stems, flowers, and vegetation. This Trial translates that mechanism into stay with a stubborn problem instead of abandoning it.

entries.title: Hold, Then Pick
entries.objective: Stay stable beside a target before making one precise collection.
entries.animalRule: Stabilize first, then make one precise pickup.
entries.userBenefit: Builds steadiness and fine motor control before action.
entries.mechanismConnection: Damselflies can maintain position beside stems and pick small insects from vegetation. This Trial translates that hover-then-take sequence into a brief steady hold followed by one precise tong pickup.

entries.title: Host a Three-Person Shared Meal
entries.objective: Create one meal where three people each contribute a different part.
entries.animalRule: Cooperation must be distributed: no single person supplies every meaningful part.
entries.userBenefit: Turns cooperation into a visible result assembled from separate contributions.
entries.mechanismConnection: Gray Wolf expresses Cooperation through this mode: Covers enormous distances at an economical trot as a family group, approaching many large prey animals in order to read which ones cannot hold their ground, and breaking off from the great majority of those encounters without an attack. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action. This Trial translates that mid mechanism into one safe, one-off human action: Host a Three-Person Shared Meal.

entries.title: Hover One Balloon Above a Mark
entries.objective: Complete one balloon above a floor mark as a one-off expression of Ease.
entries.animalRule: Use one calm attempt only; remain with the same setup until one balloon above a floor mark is complete.
entries.userBenefit: You turn ease into a concrete one-off experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Dumbo Octopus — Flapping two ear-like fins • Hovering above the mud • Swallowing prey entire: Moves by flapping paired fins mounted on an internal cartilage support rather than by jetting, hovers just above abyssal sediment, and swallows worms and crustaceans whole because its radula is reduced and it does not bite prey apart the way shallow-water octopuses do This Trial translates that low mechanism into one safe human action: Hover One Balloon Above a Mark.

entries.title: Improve One Ordinary Thing Once
entries.objective: Choose one ordinary task, object or routine you will genuinely use today and make one concrete improvement to it without expanding the job.
entries.animalRule: One improvement only, made to something you will actually use today.
entries.userBenefit: One thing you use daily is measurably better, for about five minutes of work.
entries.mechanismConnection: New Caledonian Crow — Making a Hook in Advance — Selecting a twig or a Pandanus leaf • Working it into a hooked or barbed tool away from the food • Carrying the finished tool to the prey and keeping it afterwards: Manufactures tools to a consistent design, including hooks bent into twigs and stepped barbed strips cut from Pandanus leaves, often before reaching the food and then retained, which requires the shape to be produced from a plan rather than found This Trial translates that mid-frequency mechanism into one ordinary useful thing.

entries.title: Improve One Valuable Thing Slowly
entries.objective: Invest attention where accumulated value is highest.
entries.animalRule: Work on something already valuable to you; starting a new project does not count.
entries.userBenefit: You protect accumulated value instead of constantly resetting to zero.
entries.mechanismConnection: Atlantic Cod — Scales egg production disproportionately with body size, so a large old female contributes far more, and better quality, eggs than several small ones, which makes the reproductive output of a population depend on its oldest fish rather than on its numbers. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Improvise a thirty-second silent scene
entries.objective: Improvise a thirty-second silent scene.
entries.animalRule: Preserve this Prevost's Squirrel constraint: Diverges into sharply distinct regional colour forms because large rivers and straits divide Sundaland into blocks that a tree squirrel cannot cross, so each population evolves its own pattern in isolation. Keep that limiting condition unchanged for the whole one-off action.
entries.userBenefit: You practise a concrete color signal-shaped action through a thirty-second silent scene.
entries.mechanismConnection: Prevost's Squirrel expresses Color Signal through this mode: Diverges into sharply distinct regional colour forms because large rivers and straits divide Sundaland into blocks that a tree squirrel cannot cross, so each population evolves its own pattern in isolation. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Intercept Five Flying Paper Balls
entries.objective: Turn prediction into a rapid catching challenge.
entries.animalRule: Each throw should arrive without telling you its exact direction first.
entries.userBenefit: You train reaction speed and prediction while producing a chaotic scoreable challenge.
entries.mechanismConnection: Red-footed Cannibalfly — Intercepting • Grappling • Injecting: It launches on a lead course, seizes the prey in spined legs in mid-air and drives a stiff proboscis in behind the head. Red-footed Cannibalflies are robber flies that catch other insects in flight using strong spiny legs and piercing mouthparts to subdue prey. This Trial translates that mechanism into turn prediction into a rapid catching challenge.

entries.title: Intercept the Moving Target
entries.objective: Move toward where a target will be, not where it is now.
entries.animalRule: Aim ahead of the moving ball; do not chase directly behind it.
entries.userBenefit: Trains anticipation, rapid movement and interception.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Green Darners independently control four wings and intercept prey by steering toward where it is going. This Trial safely translates that predictive interception into cutting off a rolling soft ball before an end line.

entries.title: Introduce One Competing Pattern Fast
entries.objective: Jam One Signal Under Pressure.
entries.animalRule: Your pattern must run at the same time as theirs, not in the gaps between it.
entries.userBenefit: Thirty seconds that show how hard it is to hold a pattern once something competes with it.
entries.mechanismConnection: Answers an attacking bat with ultrasonic clicks timed to interfere with its returning echoes, which degrades the bat's ranging at the moment of the strike rather than merely warning it away

entries.title: Invent a Snack From Three Ingredients
entries.objective: Adapt to what is available and make the combination actually work.
entries.animalRule: Use exactly three main ingredients.
entries.userBenefit: You practise improvisation and finish with something original you can eat.
entries.mechanismConnection: Sooty-headed Bulbul — Switching • Edge-dwelling • Sociable: A gut and bill that handle both fruit and insects let the bird track whichever is currently abundant. This bird is known for its ability to live in various habitats, using its adaptability and melodious calls to thrive in changing landscapes. This Trial translates that mechanism into adapt to what is available and make the combination actually work.

entries.title: Invent one mnemonic for five facts
entries.objective: Invent one mnemonic for five facts.
entries.animalRule: Preserve this Australasian Swamphen constraint: Uses a long unwebbed foot to grip food and lift it to the bill, which allows the bird to process tough fibrous stems and rhizomes item by item instead of swallowing whatever it can seize, and opens a food supply most waterbirds cannot use. Keep that limiting condition unchanged for the whole one-off action.
entries.userBenefit: You practise a concrete adaptable foraging-shaped action through one mnemonic for five facts.
entries.mechanismConnection: Australasian Swamphen expresses Adaptable Foraging through this mode: Uses a long unwebbed foot to grip food and lift it to the bill, which allows the bird to process tough fibrous stems and rhizomes item by item instead of swallowing whatever it can seize, and opens a food supply most waterbirds cannot use. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Invest Ten Quiet Minutes
entries.objective: Give time to something whose payoff will arrive later.
entries.animalRule: Choose delayed value over instant entertainment for the full session.
entries.userBenefit: Builds patience and long-term investment.
entries.mechanismConnection: Galápagos Tortoises survive with slow metabolism, long lifespans and patient use of scarce resources. This Trial translates that time horizon into ten quiet minutes invested in a future benefit.

entries.title: Join One Complementary Team
entries.objective: With two or more people, assign different roles for one tiny shared objective and complete it once.
entries.animalRule: Each participant must have a different role; nobody may duplicate the same job merely to finish faster.
entries.userBenefit: Practises collaboration where different methods contribute to one result without everyone competing for the same work.
entries.mechanismConnection: Oriental White-eye uses this mode by travels in flocks made of several species that each forage differently, so the group provides shared vigilance and flushed prey without the members competing for the same food

entries.title: Join One Moving Job and Add Weight
entries.objective: Add real effort to something already rolling without taking it over.
entries.animalRule: You must add to the direction already set; changing it ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: A job that was dragging finishes, and you learn how much faster things move when nobody renegotiates them.
entries.mechanismConnection: Blue Wildebeest — Collective migratory momentum. This Trial translates that collective momentum into joining a job already moving and adding weight to it.

entries.title: Join Someone's Game for Five Minutes
entries.objective: Enter an activity already happening and play alongside someone for five minutes.
entries.animalRule: Join an activity already in motion and coordinate with the group rather than starting a separate one.
entries.userBenefit: Makes coordinated group play tangible by requiring you to enter and match an existing activity.
entries.mechanismConnection: Smooth-coated Otter — Formation • Herding • Synchronised: The group swims abreast in a rough V, driving fish ahead of it into shallows or against a bank where they are concentrated enough for everyone to catch some This Trial translates that high mechanism into ten tokens into one corner.

entries.title: Jump One Line Then Brake Cleanly
entries.objective: Turn a fast jump into a controlled landing challenge.
entries.animalRule: Use a flat clear floor; the landing only counts if both feet settle without an extra step.
entries.userBenefit: You get a compact explosive challenge where control after the jump matters as much as distance.
entries.mechanismConnection: Bold Jumper — Attaches a silk dragline before jumping and controls the payout during flight, which stabilises body attitude, corrects rotation and provides a brake and a return route, turning an uncontrollable ballistic leap into a steerable one. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Keep Contact Using Only Tiny Sounds
entries.objective: Complete contact using only tiny sounds as one visible expression of Stridulation.
entries.animalRule: Exactly one attempt is allowed, and the result must preserve this constraint: digging, buzzing, regrouping.
entries.userBenefit: You practise stridulation through the unusual constraint of contact using only tiny sounds.
entries.mechanismConnection: Lowland Streaked Tenrec — Digging • Buzzing • Regrouping: The animal works damp leaf litter for earthworms nose-down and half-blind, keeping contact with its family group by vibrating a patch of specialised quills against each other to produce a train of high pulses This Trial translates that mechanism into the one-off action “Keep Contact Using Only Tiny Sounds”.

entries.title: Keep Going Through One Uncomfortable Stretch
entries.objective: Continue a task past the first point of wanting to stop.
entries.animalRule: You must continue past the first quit impulse for five continuous minutes, working through the discomfort rather than breaking off.
entries.userBenefit: You practise resilience under mild friction and discover how often the urge to stop is earlier than the real limit.
entries.mechanismConnection: Water Buffalo — Resilience under difficult conditions. This Trial translates that mechanism into continuing past the first quit point.

entries.title: Keep Moving for Five Full Minutes
entries.objective: Stay continuously active without stopping.
entries.animalRule: Movement must remain continuous for all five minutes; stopping ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: You get a simple relentless cardio burst where continuity is the entire challenge.
entries.mechanismConnection: Atlantic Mackerel — Lacks both a swim bladder and the ability to pump water over its gills, so it must keep moving to breathe and to stay off the bottom, which makes continuous swimming a requirement of the anatomy rather than a behaviour. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Keep One Ancient Habit Alive
entries.objective: Preserve one old technique that still earns its place.
entries.animalRule: The old method must do the whole job; reaching for the modern version partway ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: One skill you still have stays usable, instead of quietly becoming something you used to be able to do.
entries.mechanismConnection: Cuban Solenodon — Grooved-Incisor Venom Delivery — Nocturnal • Rooting • Solitary: Works leaf litter at night with a flexible snout and subdues prey through venomous saliva channelled along a groove in the lower incisor This Trial turns that low-frequency mechanism into one old useful method.

entries.title: Keep One Queue With Visible Gaps
entries.objective: Keep One Queue With Visible Gaps.
entries.animalRule: Each step down must be visibly smaller than the one before it; two equal gaps end the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: You practise maintaining order by respecting the space between ranks rather than competing for the same slot.
entries.mechanismConnection: Maintains a strict size-based queue within one coral head in which each individual keeps its size a measured step below the one above, so growth is regulated socially rather than by food, and removing one fish moves everyone up a rank

entries.title: Keep One Resource for Fifteen Minutes
entries.objective: Defend one useful resource from casual interruption for a short window.
entries.animalRule: The resource stays dedicated to one purpose for the full fifteen minutes.
entries.userBenefit: You experience what a protected resource can produce when it is not constantly shared or interrupted.
entries.mechanismConnection: Mistle Thrush — Defends an individual fruiting tree as an exclusive winter food store, attacking redwings, fieldfares and other thrushes that approach, which converts a shared resource into a private one at the cost of constant defence through the whole winter. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Keep One Useful Thing Growing
entries.objective: Improve something that already works instead of replacing it.
entries.animalRule: Preserve the existing working core; the Trial is an addition, not a rebuild.
entries.userBenefit: You practise compounding a working system instead of restarting from zero.
entries.mechanismConnection: American Lobster — Keeps moulting and growing indefinitely rather than reaching a terminal size, and maintains telomerase activity in somatic tissue, so reproductive output and condition continue rising with age instead of declining, which makes the oldest animals the most productive. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Keep One Valuable Thing Untouched
entries.objective: Guard one useful resource through a short period of deliberate non-use.
entries.animalRule: The protected resource remains completely unused for the full fifteen minutes.
entries.userBenefit: You practise carrying value through a vulnerable window instead of consuming it just because it is available.
entries.mechanismConnection: Asian Arowana — Incubates a small clutch of very large eggs inside the male's mouth for weeks, during which he cannot feed, which converts an enormous per-egg investment into fry that emerge already large and capable rather than into numbers. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Kick One Tower at Its Weak Point
entries.objective: Build one freestanding tower from light household objects, identify its weakest point, then destroy it with one kick.
entries.animalRule: Preserve this Secretarybird constraint: Secretarybird — Stilt-Leg Stomp Strike — Stamping • Precise • Milliseconds: Delivers a kick of several times body weight onto a snake's head in about fifteen milliseconds. Keep that limiting condition unchanged for the whole one-off action.
entries.userBenefit: Practises structural reasoning followed by decisive force and produces an unusually satisfying proof moment.
entries.mechanismConnection: Secretarybird expresses Specific Force through this mode: Secretarybird — Stilt-Leg Stomp Strike — Stamping • Precise • Milliseconds: Delivers a kick of several times body weight onto a snake's head in about fifteen milliseconds. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Label One Real Protective Feature
entries.objective: Create a bold warning label for a genuinely useful protective feature—such as a sealed case, password lock, or spill tray—and photograph both together.
entries.animalRule: The warning may only claim a protection that is actually present and demonstrable; no fake danger or threat is allowed.
entries.userBenefit: Practises credible signalling by pairing a conspicuous warning with a real underlying safeguard instead of empty display.
entries.mechanismConnection: Devil's Coach Horse Beetle uses this mode by backs the posture with a real chemical deterrent, so the bluff is not empty even though the sting it imitates does not exist

entries.title: Launch From Stillness to One Marker
entries.objective: Launch From Stillness to One Marker.
entries.animalRule: You must be completely still until the signal, and stop under control rather than running through.
entries.userBenefit: You feel the contrast between loaded stillness and a single explosive launch.
entries.mechanismConnection: Accelerates by loading the whole body into an S and straightening it in one contraction, which converts the entire trunk into a single-stroke launcher and makes the strike faster than any predator could react to

entries.title: Launch One Towel in One Burst
entries.objective: Turn stored force into one brief, complete action.
entries.animalRule: You get one push only; do not chase, kick, or touch the towel again after release.
entries.userBenefit: You practise committing force cleanly instead of leaking effort through repeated corrections.
entries.mechanismConnection: American Crocodile — Lunging • Explosive • Brief: A tail built for one enormous thrust drives a strike that is over in under a second, after which the animal returns to doing nothing This Trial translates that high mechanism into one towel across a line.

entries.title: Launch Three Precision Jumps
entries.objective: Launch Three Precision Jumps.
entries.animalRule: Each landing must come to a controlled stop before the next jump begins.
entries.userBenefit: Three clean landings, and a real sense of what your body will and will not commit to.
entries.mechanismConnection: Jumps by forcing body fluid into its legs to straighten them rather than by muscular extension, which produces a leap many times its length from a body with no extensor muscles in those joints

entries.title: Layer Two Voices at Once
entries.objective: Record yourself producing two contrasting rhythmic or vocal parts layered into one 15-second performance using any simple recording tool.
entries.animalRule: The final proof must contain two simultaneous parts created by you; a single melody played twice in sequence does not count.
entries.userBenefit: Develops coordination and expressive range by combining independent parts into one coherent performance.
entries.mechanismConnection: White-rumped Shama uses this mode by sings with two independently controlled halves of one vocal organ, so a single bird produces two notes at once and can overlap, harmonise and switch between voices in a way no animal with a larynx can

entries.title: Learn One Skill Directly From Someone
entries.objective: Copy one small skill from a person who already knows how to do it.
entries.animalRule: Learn socially by observing what already works, trying it, and retaining the correction that improves your result.
entries.userBenefit: Turns adaptive social learning into a fast real-world transfer of know-how.
entries.mechanismConnection: Long-tailed Macaque — Working whatever the site offers • Copying what pays • Testing the boundary: Runs one opportunistic foraging system whose targets are learned locally, so coastal troops crack shellfish with stones while temple troops take objects from visitors and trade them back for food, both acquired the same way and both maintained by copying This Trial translates that mid mechanism into one safe human action: Try Three Methods Then Keep One.

entries.title: Learn to Juggle Three Objects
entries.objective: Reach three consecutive controlled catches in a three-object cascade.
entries.animalRule: Experiment rapidly with throw height and timing, changing one thing at a time until the pattern stabilises.
entries.userBenefit: Turns experimentation into immediate visible motor learning.
entries.mechanismConnection: Olive Baboon expresses Experimentation through this mode: Tests unfamiliar food and unfamiliar problems in front of fifty or more animals who are watching, which turns a single individual's success into something the whole troop adopts within a season without anyone else paying the cost of discovering it. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action. This Trial translates that mid mechanism into one safe, one-off human action: Learn to Juggle Three Objects.

entries.title: Leave One Activity on Your Own Cue
entries.objective: Walk out of something still running, at a moment you pick rather than one you are given.
entries.animalRule: The activity must still be running when you go; leaving at its natural end does not count.
entries.userBenefit: You get back the time you normally lose waiting for someone else to declare a thing finished.
entries.mechanismConnection: Domestic Cat — Self-determined engagement. This Trial translates that self-determined engagement into leaving something while it is still running.

entries.title: Leave One Shared Space When Signaled
entries.objective: Respond quickly to one clear sign that a shared space is not suitable.
entries.animalRule: The signal must be agreed first; leave on the first signal without asking for an explanation.
entries.userBenefit: You practise a clean low-drama boundary that can make shared spaces easier to use.
entries.mechanismConnection: Caribbean Spiny Lobster — Detects a chemical signal released by lobsters infected with a lethal virus and avoids sharing shelter with them, which breaks transmission in a species that otherwise gains from sheltering together, so the social habit and the defence against it run on the same chemistry. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Let One Warm Object Cool Naturally
entries.objective: Complete one warm object cool naturally as one visible expression of Heat Endurance.
entries.animalRule: Exactly one attempt is allowed, and the result must preserve this constraint: storing heat by day, grazing, dumping it at night.
entries.userBenefit: You practise heat endurance through the unusual constraint of one warm object cool naturally.
entries.mechanismConnection: East African Oryx — Storing heat by day • Grazing • Dumping it at night: A network of fine arteries at the base of the skull passes blood to the brain through venous blood cooled in the nasal passages, so the brain can be held at a safe temperature while the rest of the body is allowed to climb several degrees, storing heat instead of spending water to shed it This Trial translates that mechanism into the one-off action “Let One Warm Object Cool Naturally”.

entries.title: Let Three Chances Pass Take the Fourth
entries.objective: Deliberately waste three good openings to find out what a better one looks like.
entries.animalRule: You must let exactly three go; taking an earlier one ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: You get a concrete feel for the difference between the first opening and a better one.
entries.mechanismConnection: Saltwater Crocodile — Ambush timing. This Trial translates that mechanism into delaying until a better opening. This Trial translates that ambush patience into three chances deliberately let go before the fourth.

entries.title: Listen from the Edge for Ten Minutes
entries.objective: Sit at the boundary of activity and only listen.
entries.animalRule: You must remain at the edge and produce no action beyond listening.
entries.userBenefit: You practise edge listening and notice how much information arrives when you stop being part of the action.
entries.mechanismConnection: Buffy Fish Owl — Waterside listening and waiting. This Trial translates that mechanism into edge-based pure listening.

entries.title: Load One Kit Before The Crossing
entries.objective: Load One Kit Before The Crossing.
entries.animalRule: Nothing may be fetched once you have moved away from the supply area.
entries.userBenefit: Ten minutes of work with nothing missing, and a clear list of what you actually needed.
entries.mechanismConnection: Loads fat at a stopover until its body mass rises far above normal, then crosses a barrier with no food or water on reserves alone, so the crossing is decided by the quality of the stopover rather than by the flight

entries.title: Locate One Hidden Sound Source Set37
entries.objective: Complete one hidden sound source as one visible expression of Marsh Patience.
entries.animalRule: Exactly one attempt is allowed; preserve the animal-derived constraint: striding shallows, taking what appears, nesting very high.
entries.userBenefit: You practise marsh patience through a concrete one-off challenge with a clear finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Lesser Adjutant Stork — Striding shallows • Taking what appears • Nesting very high: The wetland it feeds in is widespread and the thing it actually runs short of is the nest site, since a colony needs emergent trees tall and strong enough to carry heavy platforms, and those are the first thing removed from a farmed landscape This Trial translates that low mechanism into one safe, one-off human action: Locate One Hidden Sound Source Set37.

entries.title: Locate One Hidden String by Listening
entries.objective: Complete one hidden string by listening as a one-off expression of Seasonal Signal.
entries.animalRule: Complete exactly one uninterrupted attempt; do not switch activities until one hidden string by listening is complete.
entries.userBenefit: You turn seasonal signal into a concrete one-off experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: American Robin — Head cocked sideways • Listening for movement below • Pulling: Locates earthworms in soil primarily by sound rather than sight, which is why it works open short grass in a series of runs and pauses with the head turned to one side, then strikes directly at a worm it has never seen This Trial translates that mid mechanism into one safe human action: Locate One Hidden String by Listening.

entries.title: Lower Your Effort for Five Minutes
entries.objective: Deliberately reduce movement and breathing pace for one quiet reset.
entries.animalRule: Stay seated and leave the phone untouched for the full five minutes.
entries.userBenefit: You practise dropping energy demand instead of fighting fatigue with more stimulation.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Frog — Overwinters submerged in pond mud taking oxygen entirely across the skin from the water, with metabolism suppressed far enough that cutaneous exchange alone is sufficient, which requires the water to stay oxygenated throughout. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Lunge Once at an Unseen Sound
entries.objective: Turn on a sound you cannot see and commit to one lunge.
entries.animalRule: One lunge only, and your eyes stay shut until your hand lands.
entries.userBenefit: A three-second burst that shows how accurately you can place a sound when you have to commit.
entries.mechanismConnection: Tiger Wolf Spider — Tremor-Cued Night Lunge — Turning • Lunging • Holding: Converts a vibration bearing into a single committed lunge of a few body lengths, seizing the prey directly with the legs and fangs because there is no web to do any part of the work This Trial translates that vibration bearing turned into a single committed lunge into one blind lunge at a tapped spot.

entries.title: Make a Gift From What You Own
entries.objective: Create one gift without buying any new materials.
entries.animalRule: Provision the finished gift entirely from resources already gathered and available to you.
entries.userBenefit: Turns existing resources into a deliberate provision for someone else.
entries.mechanismConnection: Blue Mud Dauber expresses Solitary Provision through this mode: Takes over the abandoned mud nests of other wasps rather than building from scratch, carrying water in its crop to soften the old mud and reshape it, then stocking each cell with spiders it has stung into paralysis rather than killed so the food is still alive when the larva reaches it. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Make a Water Wheel Turn
entries.objective: Build a small wheel that visibly rotates when a controlled stream of water hits it.
entries.animalRule: The wheel must hold its position while moving water passes through it; rotation comes from the current rather than from your hand.
entries.userBenefit: You discover there is a still place in a busy room, and where it is in the rooms you use most.
entries.mechanismConnection: Giant Stonefly — Flattened, clinging and oxygen-hungry: a body pressed flat against stone sits inside the thin slow layer at the riverbed, where tufted gills take oxygen from water moving fast enough to carry plenty of it. This Trial translates that low mechanism into one safe, one-off human action: Make a Water Wheel Turn.

entries.title: Make One Angle-Stable Blue
entries.objective: Create or find a non-iridescent blue object and photograph it from three viewing angles in one collage to show the colour staying stable.
entries.animalRule: Use one blue surface only; it must remain recognisably the same colour from all three angles rather than relying on a changing reflective effect.
entries.userBenefit: You can tell structural colour from pigment on sight, which changes how you look at everything iridescent.
entries.mechanismConnection: Asian Fairy-bluebird uses this mode by produces blue from a spongy disordered nanostructure rather than from stacked layers, so the colour is the same from every direction instead of flashing and shifting as iridescent colour does

entries.title: Make One Cut That Repeats Everywhere
entries.objective: Make One Cut That Repeats Everywhere.
entries.animalRule: One cut only, made while the sheet is still folded; opening it to correct the shape ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: You get an immediate visual lesson in how one action at the centre can multiply across a whole structure.
entries.mechanismConnection: Bores through the folded heart of a palm so that one tunnel is replicated across every frond as the leaves expand, which multiplies the damage from a single boring into months of lost photosynthesis

entries.title: Make One Detail Impossible to Miss
entries.objective: Choose one useful object, note or feature and change its presentation so it becomes the first thing a viewer notices.
entries.animalRule: Only the presentation may change; the object itself must stay exactly as it was.
entries.userBenefit: The thing you keep missing becomes the first thing you see, without a reminder app.
entries.mechanismConnection: Golden Tortoise Beetle — Colour Changed by Moving Water — Reflecting gold from a fluid-filled multilayer cuticle • Draining the layers when disturbed • Turning red as the mirror collapses: Holds a stack of transparent cuticle layers separated by fluid that acts as an optical mirror producing metallic gold, and can withdraw the fluid so the layers collapse and the structural colour fails, revealing red pigment beneath This Trial translates that mid-frequency mechanism into one high-contrast useful detail.

entries.title: Make One Holder From a Single Material
entries.objective: Build a useful support without shopping for components.
entries.animalRule: The holder's structure must come from one material only.
entries.userBenefit: You discover how far one material can go when the design does the work.
entries.mechanismConnection: Edible-nest Swiftlet — Builds a nest from hardened salivary secretion alone, with no plant material at all, which allows a bird that never lands on the ground and cannot perch to attach a nest to a sheer cave wall in complete darkness. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Make One Meal Entirely From Fruit
entries.objective: Prepare and eat one complete meal made only from fruit.
entries.animalRule: The feeding event must remain entirely fruit-based while drawing from several fruit sources.
entries.userBenefit: Turns specialized fruit feeding into one bounded, visible meal rather than an all-day diet rule.
entries.mechanismConnection: Jambu Fruit Dove expresses Canopy-Green Stillness through this mode: Swallows fruit whole and voids the seeds intact elsewhere, so the width of its gape determines which tree species are dispersed at all and which are left to drop beneath their parent. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Make One Pattern Read Two Ways
entries.objective: Create a visual that changes between distance and close-up.
entries.animalRule: The same sheet must show a bold distant shape and a different close-up texture.
entries.userBenefit: You create a simple visual illusion that rewards both first glance and inspection.
entries.mechanismConnection: Silver Pheasant — Carries a plumage built from white feathers each finely vermiculated with black, so the same bird reads as a striking white shape across a dim forest floor and as an intricate pattern at close range, which lets one signal work at two very different distances. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Make One Person Notice First
entries.objective: Introduce one visible unusual detail without announcing it and continue normally until somebody notices.
entries.animalRule: You may not announce it or draw attention to it; it has to be spotted unprompted.
entries.userBenefit: You learn how long an obvious change goes unmentioned, which is far longer than anyone expects.
entries.mechanismConnection: Red Paper Wasp — An Open Comb, No Envelope — Chewing wood fibre into paper • Building a single uncovered comb on a stalk • Defending it with bodies rather than with a wall: Builds one exposed comb hung from a short stalk with no paper envelope around it, which keeps construction cheap and the brood visible to the adults but leaves defence entirely to the wasps themselves This Trial translates that mid-frequency mechanism into one unannounced visible detail.

entries.title: Make One Photo Then Delete It
entries.objective: Create one deliberately good photo whose value exists only in the moment.
entries.animalRule: Commit to the performance rather than keeping the artifact: one polished attempt, one viewing, then release it.
entries.userBenefit: Separates the act of making something well from the urge to keep or post it.
entries.mechanismConnection: Racket-tailed Roller expresses Aerial Acrobatics through this mode: Displays by diving and rolling in barely controlled flight close to the ground, which cannot be performed by a bird in poor condition and therefore demonstrates capability rather than merely claiming it. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Make One Promise and Show the Work
entries.objective: Make One Promise and Show the Work.
entries.animalRule: You may only promise what you can finish now, and the result has to be where they can check it.
entries.userBenefit: You connect a visible signal of reliability to actual service.
entries.mechanismConnection: Advertises paternal quality with snout tentacles resembling a brood of larvae and then delivers on that signal by guarding the eggs alone in a cave, which ties the ornament directly to the service it advertises

entries.title: Make One Recipe With What Exists
entries.objective: Adapt one simple food or drink to the ingredients actually available.
entries.animalRule: Use only what is already available; the substitute must serve the missing ingredient's function.
entries.userBenefit: You practise adapting the system to local resources instead of abandoning the result when one input is missing.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Wall Lizard — Runs a generalist lizard that adjusts its diet to local supply, and on one Adriatic islet an introduced population shifted from insects to plants and evolved caecal valves and altered head shape within about thirty years, showing how quickly the digestive system can be remodelled. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Make One Scraps-Only Snack
entries.objective: Make One Scraps-Only Snack.
entries.animalRule: Nothing may be bought, and every component must already have been destined for the bin.
entries.userBenefit: You extract value from food that would otherwise be ignored.
entries.mechanismConnection: Processes sediment and detritus with a muscular grinding stomach and an extremely long gut, which lets a large fish live on material with almost no nutritional value that nothing else is competing for

entries.title: Make One Shadow-Puppet Scene
entries.objective: Create a short recognisable scene using only shadows and a light source.
entries.animalRule: Let the visible result come from silhouette rather than the object itself; the light stays behind the performers.
entries.userBenefit: Turns shadow control into a small visual performance.
entries.mechanismConnection: Indochinese Tiger — Holding a huge territory • One large kill • Days at the carcass: A tiger needs a standing population of deer and pig across hundreds of square kilometres, and industrial-scale wire snaring removes that prey base first, so forests across its range now look complete from the air and contain almost no animals at ground level This Trial translates that low mechanism into one safe, one-off human action: Make One Shadow-Puppet Scene.

entries.title: Make One Snack From Mixed Scraps
entries.objective: Make One Snack From Mixed Scraps.
entries.animalRule: Exactly three components, all already in the house, and nothing bought to bind them.
entries.userBenefit: You rescue usable food and practise getting value from materials that normally do not belong together.
entries.mechanismConnection: Ingests solid food, which no spider or scorpion can do, because the mouthparts and gut handle particles rather than requiring external digestion, so the animal eats carrion, fungi, droppings and plant matter as well as prey

entries.title: Make One Snack From Overlooked Food
entries.objective: Turn one ignored edible ingredient into something worth eating.
entries.animalRule: The overlooked ingredient has to be the main feature, not a garnish.
entries.userBenefit: You turn something easy to ignore into useful food and practise seeing value before it is wasted.
entries.mechanismConnection: Eurasian Bullfinch — Feeds on the dormant flower buds of trees through late winter when nothing else is available, stripping them at a rate of hundreds a day with a broad rounded bill, which converts an unused winter resource into food at the cost of the following season's blossom. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Make One Startling Rattle Fast
entries.objective: Build and perform a harmless sound warning.
entries.animalRule: The container has to stay closed during the performance; one five-second burst only.
entries.userBenefit: You get a ridiculous miniature performance and a homemade sound object worth replaying.
entries.mechanismConnection: California Spiny Lobster — Produces sound by drawing a soft tissue plectrum across a ridged file, a stick-slip mechanism that needs no hard rubbing surfaces, so the animal can still deter and startle a predator during the days after moulting when everything else about it is soft. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Make One Stranger-Looking Combination Work
entries.objective: Combine two ordinary things that do not normally belong together and make the result genuinely useful.
entries.animalRule: The two must be used together on one real task; testing them separately ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: One combination that works, which you would never have tried if it had to look sensible first.
entries.mechanismConnection: Harris's Hawk — Relayed Flush and Ambush — Stacked perching • Leapfrogging • Watching one another: A stable family party of two to six moves through desert scrub by leapfrogging between lookouts and keeping every bird in sight of the others, which is the standing arrangement that makes a joint attack possible at any moment This Trial translates that mid mechanism into one unlikely useful pairing.

entries.title: Make One Surface Shed Liquid
entries.objective: Make One Surface Shed Liquid.
entries.animalRule: The untreated half must stay untouched as a control, and both must be tested in one go.
entries.userBenefit: You end up knowing which surface treatment actually sheds liquid, having seen both side by side.
entries.mechanismConnection: Coats itself with self-made protein nanoparticles that create a surface too rough at a microscopic scale for liquid to wet, which stops the sugary sap it excretes from fouling its own body

entries.title: Make One Thing From What Is Here
entries.objective: Produce something whose whole appearance is decided by what happened to be available.
entries.animalRule: Nothing may be fetched from another room or bought; what is in reach is the whole palette.
entries.userBenefit: You end up with something real and a much better sense of what is actually lying around you.
entries.mechanismConnection: House Finch — Red That Must Be Eaten — Feeding on seeds, buds and fruit • Depositing dietary carotenoids into growing feathers at the moult • Wearing a colour that reports what was available: Deposits carotenoid pigments it cannot synthesise into the feathers it grows at moult, so the intensity of a male's red is set by what he managed to eat and how healthy he was at that time, making the colour an unfakeable record This Trial translates that carotenoid colour reporting the diet into an object whose materials were whatever was in reach.

entries.title: Make One Thing Unpleasant to Pick Up
entries.objective: Protect something by making it unappealing rather than by hiding it.
entries.animalRule: It must stay in plain view and must remain completely safe to touch.
entries.userBenefit: The thing stays where you put it without a lock, a label or a conversation.
entries.mechanismConnection: Southern Toad — Glands Loaded With Cardiac Poison — Sitting still when approached • Secreting a milky toxin from glands behind the eyes • Relying on the attacker releasing it rather than on escape: Carries paired parotoid glands behind the head that release bufadienolides, compounds that act on the heart muscle of a vertebrate, so the response to a predator is to stay in place and let the mouth that closes on it do the work This Trial translates that parotoid toxin relied on in the open into an object made unappealing rather than hidden.

entries.title: Make One Tool From Scrap
entries.objective: Solve a small physical problem by inventing the tool first.
entries.animalRule: The final solution has to use the tool you made rather than your bare hand.
entries.userBenefit: You practise general problem-solving by inventing the missing tool instead of searching for one.
entries.mechanismConnection: Goffin's Cockatoo — Solves novel physical problems by manufacturing tools despite having no tool use at all in the wild, which means the capability is general problem-solving applied to objects rather than the execution of an inherited behaviour. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Make Something Useful From Packaging
entries.objective: Turn discarded material into a practical object.
entries.animalRule: The finished object must have a clear practical use.
entries.userBenefit: You practise improvisation, reduce waste, and finish with a useful object made from almost nothing.
entries.mechanismConnection: Epaulette Shark — Walking • Tolerant • Shutting down: Muscular paired fins carry it across exposed reef between pools, and it can shut down non-essential brain function to survive oxygen levels that would kill most fish. Epaulette Sharks can use paired fins to walk or crawl over reef flats and tide pools, and tolerate low-oxygen conditions during low tides. This Trial translates that mechanism into turn discarded material into a practical object.

entries.title: Make the Loudest Rhythm From One Object
entries.objective: Make the Loudest Rhythm From One Object.
entries.animalRule: One object only, and nothing breakable, no person and no animal may be struck.
entries.userBenefit: A tiny source becomes a surprisingly big performance.
entries.mechanismConnection: Produces sound by snapping ribbed membranes in and out hundreds of times a second and amplifying the clicks in a hollow abdomen, which generates one of the loudest calls in the insect world from a very small body

entries.title: Make Three Passes Around Four Obstacles
entries.objective: Dash One Zigzag Course.
entries.animalRule: All three passes must stay on your feet with no gliding stops between obstacles.
entries.userBenefit: Three fast controlled passes, and a clear sense of where your balance actually gives out.
entries.mechanismConnection: Carries a heavy body on small wings, which makes gliding impossible and forces continuous rapid beating, producing a flight too fast and too abrupt for a bird to intercept

entries.title: Map Five Things You Rely On
entries.objective: Make a quick map of the resources you already know well.
entries.animalRule: Mark the five locations from memory first; checking comes only after the map is finished.
entries.userBenefit: You expose how well you actually know the territory you depend on every day.
entries.mechanismConnection: Marsh Tit — Holds a single large territory year-round as a lifelong pair, which gives complete knowledge of the cache sites, food sources and cavities within it, and makes the pair's survival depend entirely on that one patch of woodland. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Map One Human-Made Habitat
entries.objective: Find three human-made features in one area that an animal could plausibly use for shelter, perching, or nesting, without disturbing wildlife.
entries.animalRule: Observe only: do not touch nests, animals, or occupied shelter; all three features must be human-made structures.
entries.userBenefit: You start seeing the built world the way something living in it would, which you cannot really switch off afterwards.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Pheasant uses this mode by exists in the countryside as an annually released population rather than a self-sustaining wild one, so its numbers, timing and ecological effects are set by rearing and release decisions rather than by anything the species does

entries.title: Mark One Boundary Without Building It
entries.objective: Mark One Boundary Without Building It.
entries.animalRule: Only a marker may define the edge; building a physical barrier ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: A clear boundary protects space without needing a wall.
entries.mechanismConnection: Holds reef space chemically by carrying palytoxin, one of the most poisonous non-protein compounds known, so an animal with no skeleton and no aggression keeps ground against organisms that could overgrow it

entries.title: Mark One Good Year on a Timeline
entries.objective: Turn one period of your life into a visible record of conditions.
entries.animalRule: Use the same visual scale for all five years before adding explanations.
entries.userBenefit: You create a compact physical-looking archive of how conditions changed over time.
entries.mechanismConnection: Dall Sheep — Grows horn at a rate that tracks nutrition, so growth almost stops each winter and leaves a distinct annulus, and the spacing between annuli records how good each year was, making the horn a physical archive of the animal's whole life. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Mark One Hazard for the Next Person
entries.objective: Turn one bad experience of your own into a warning for people who were not there.
entries.animalRule: The warning must sit on the thing itself, and it must make sense to a person who was not there when it went wrong.
entries.userBenefit: The next person, including future you, stops repeating a mistake nobody had written down.
entries.mechanismConnection: American Crow — Remembering a Face, Telling Others — Learning the face of a person who threatened it • Scolding that face on sight for years • Passing the association to birds that never saw the event: Stores individual human faces as dangerous after a single bad encounter, then mobs and scolds that face on later sightings, and the response spreads horizontally and vertically through the local population to birds with no direct experience of it This Trial translates that single-encounter face memory passed to birds that never saw it into a warning left for people who were not there.

entries.title: Mark One Space Without a Word
entries.objective: Claim a working space so clearly that nobody has to be told.
entries.animalRule: The boundary must hold on the arrangement alone; if you have to explain it, it has not worked.
entries.userBenefit: You get an uninterrupted stretch without the awkward conversation that usually buys it.
entries.mechanismConnection: Mute Swan — Silent but firm territorial grace. This Trial translates that silent but firm territorial grace into a boundary held by arrangement alone.

entries.title: Mark One Tiny Square as Yours
entries.objective: Complete one tiny work square as a one-off expression of Pocket Territory.
entries.animalRule: Use one calm attempt only; remain with the same setup until one tiny work square is complete.
entries.userBenefit: You turn pocket territory into a concrete one-off experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Vampire Crab — Holding a few square metres • Carrying large eggs • Hatching finished crabs: Has abandoned the marine larval stage entirely, carrying a small clutch of large eggs that hatch as fully formed miniature crabs rather than as plankton, which removes any need to reach the sea and lets the whole life cycle happen in a few metres of forest stream This Trial translates that low mechanism into one safe human action: Mark One Tiny Square as Yours.

entries.title: Match One Moving Background
entries.objective: Stand near moving curtains, leaves, or another harmless moving background and gently match its rhythm for 20 seconds.
entries.animalRule: You must move only when the background moves and freeze when it settles; do not create the background movement yourself.
entries.userBenefit: Sharpens environmental timing by matching surrounding motion rather than treating stillness as the only form of concealment.
entries.mechanismConnection: Stick Mantis uses this mode by rocks gently while stationary so that its movement matches the vegetation around it, because in air that is moving everything else, holding perfectly still is what a searching predator would notice

entries.title: Match One Object to One Exact Surface
entries.objective: Match One Object to One Exact Surface.
entries.animalRule: It must be the single closest surface you can find, not merely a similar one.
entries.userBenefit: You train yourself to notice fine-grained environmental fit.
entries.mechanismConnection: Matches the specific granite and lichen pattern of its own outcrop rather than a general background, so concealment works only on the rock the population occupies and ties each population to its own stone

entries.title: Match One Person's Register Exactly Once
entries.objective: Answer someone in precisely the form they used, once, and see what it does.
entries.animalRule: The match happens exactly once and must mirror the form, not the content.
entries.userBenefit: You get a usable read on how much of a conversation's temperature is set by form rather than words.
entries.mechanismConnection: Song Sparrow — A Repertoire Learned Next Door — Learning several song types as a young bird • Matching the type a neighbour just sang • Escalating or retreating on the basis of the match: Learns a small repertoire of distinct song types from the birds around it and then uses which type it sings as a graded signal, matching a rival's song to escalate a dispute and switching away to de-escalate This Trial translates that song-type matching between neighbours into one reply mirroring the form it answers.

entries.title: Match One Surface Using Three Tones
entries.objective: Reproduce the visual grain of a nearby surface.
entries.animalRule: Use exactly three visual tones taken from the chosen surface.
entries.userBenefit: You train your eye to see contrast structure instead of naming one overall colour.
entries.mechanismConnection: Brill — Adjusts skin pattern to match the substrate by moving pigment within chromatophores under direct nervous control, using visual input, so the fish reproduces not only the colour but the grain and contrast of whatever it has settled on. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Match One Task to Today's Resources
entries.objective: Adjust effort to what is actually abundant right now.
entries.animalRule: Choose the task only after rating all three available resources.
entries.userBenefit: You practise letting current conditions choose the job instead of forcing a fixed plan.
entries.mechanismConnection: Bank Vole — Runs a population that oscillates over a few years rather than staying steady, because breeding tracks tree seed and berry crops that themselves fluctuate, and the predators that build up on high vole numbers then act on the collapse. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Match Three Warning Colors on Paper
entries.objective: Complete three warning colors on paper as a one-off expression of False Warning.
entries.animalRule: Use one calm attempt only; remain with the same setup until three warning colors on paper is complete.
entries.userBenefit: You turn false warning into a concrete one-off experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Milk Snake — Moving at night • Wearing a warning it cannot back • Constricting what it finds: Carries red, black and pale banding resembling the venomous coral snakes it shares ground with, and because the resemblance is only worth anything where predators have learned to avoid the real thing, the pattern is most precise near the model's range and degrades away from it This Trial translates that low mechanism into one safe human action: Match Three Warning Colors on Paper.

entries.title: Memorize Someone's Outfit
entries.objective: Observe one person's outfit briefly, then recall its details after looking away.
entries.animalRule: Acquire a visible pattern accurately enough to reproduce its defining details after the model is no longer visible.
entries.userBenefit: Turns visual pattern retention into a concrete observation-and-recall challenge.
entries.mechanismConnection: Postman Butterfly — Wearing another species' pattern • Both being genuinely toxic • Sharing the cost of teaching: Converges on the same red-and-black wing pattern as an unrelated distasteful longwing across the whole of its range, so that a predator learning to avoid either one has learned to avoid both, which splits the cost of educating naive birds between two species This Trial translates that mid mechanism into one safe human action: Teach One Safe Pattern by Matching.

entries.title: Merge Two Things You Keep Apart
entries.objective: Collapse the boundary between two collections that should never have been separate.
entries.animalRule: The old boundary must disappear entirely; keeping the empty second place ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: You stop checking two places for one thing, which is a cost you pay every single day.
entries.mechanismConnection: Red Imported Fire Ant — One Gene Region, Two Colonies — Dozens or hundreds of queens in one network • No aggression between neighbouring nests • Spread by budding rather than flight: Runs the many-queen form, in which workers accept multiple queens, colony boundaries dissolve into interconnected supercolonies and new nests are budded off next door, producing mound densities several times higher This Trial translates that many-queen supercolony with no boundaries between nests into two kept-apart collections merged.

entries.title: Mirror a Friend for Sixty Seconds
entries.objective: Practise rapid body adaptation by following another person's changing movement.
entries.animalRule: Stay responsive to the leader's changing direction without planning the sequence in advance.
entries.userBenefit: You train coordination, attention, reaction speed, and nonverbal rapport with another person.
entries.mechanismConnection: California Sea Lion — Manoeuvring • Pursuing • Whisker-guided: Long front flippers row and bank the body so direction can change faster than prey can. California Sea Lions are agile marine mammals that use strong front flippers for maneuvering and sensitive whiskers to detect movement while hunting fish and navigating through water. This Trial translates that mechanism into practise rapid body adaptation by following another person's changing movement.

entries.title: Mobilise One Team Fast
entries.objective: Mobilise One Team Fast.
entries.animalRule: The result must be beyond what one person could manage in three minutes.
entries.userBenefit: Three minutes produce something no one person could have built in three minutes.
entries.mechanismConnection: Operates as a large coordinated society consuming enormous resources, which exists for a single season and leaves nothing behind but mated queens

entries.title: Move Back and Raise One Barrier
entries.objective: Make one ordinary retreat motion also move a harmless barrier into place.

entries.userBenefit: You design a movement that solves two problems at once: leaving and protecting the space behind you.
entries.mechanismConnection: Blue Tang — Carries a sharp bony spine hinged into a groove on each side of the caudal peduncle that folds flat while swimming and swings out when the fish flexes its tail, turning an ordinary escape movement into a cutting strike. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Move Between Shade and Light Five Times
entries.objective: Move Between Shade and Light Five Times.
entries.animalRule: You must complete a movement at every stop, and may not cross without pausing in each.
entries.userBenefit: You get a concrete, memorable result while practising sun-rock speckle as a real human action.
entries.mechanismConnection: Brazilian Lava Lizard — Regulates body temperature by shuttling between sunlit and shaded surfaces and by altering posture and orientation, which holds a narrow internal range using position rather than metabolism and makes the animal's whole day a sequence of thermal decisions The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Move One Group In Sync
entries.objective: Move One Group In Sync.
entries.animalRule: Nobody may call the moves aloud once the sequence starts.
entries.userBenefit: Sixty seconds of people moving together without anyone calling it, which is harder and funnier than it sounds.
entries.mechanismConnection: Operates as a flock rather than as individuals, arriving at a flowering tree in hundreds, exhausting it and moving on together, so the unit that finds and uses a patchy resource is the whole group

entries.title: Move One Item Through Two Zones
entries.objective: Create a simple handoff between two different conditions.
entries.animalRule: The object must cross two distinct zones with one visible handoff point between them.
entries.userBenefit: You turn an ordinary transfer into a simple system for moving things reliably between spaces.
entries.mechanismConnection: Amano Shrimp — Runs an amphidromous life cycle in which adults live in fresh water but larvae only develop in brackish or salt water, so every generation depends on an unobstructed passage downstream and back again. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Move One Object Without Lifting It
entries.objective: Translate a movement method to a surface it was not designed for.
entries.animalRule: The object must advance through the two supports; direct hand-carrying does not count.
entries.userBenefit: You practise adapting a movement pattern when the normal mode is unavailable.
entries.mechanismConnection: Walking Catfish — Uses locked pectoral fin spines as fixed props while flexing the body, which converts a swimming stroke into terrestrial movement, supported by a branched suprabranchial organ that lets the animal breathe air for as long as the journey takes. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Move One Predictable Item Tonight
entries.objective: Break one pattern that makes something too easy to find.
entries.animalRule: Move only a nonessential personal item and choose a usable new location, not a hiding place.
entries.userBenefit: You notice how predictability creates vulnerability while improving one storage choice.
entries.mechanismConnection: European Spiny Lobster — Occupies and returns to specific shelters on rocky reef over long periods, so the animal's position is predictable across years, which is efficient while the shelter is secure and catastrophic once anyone knows where it is. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Move One Setup to a Cooler Spot
entries.objective: Improve a workspace or rest spot by changing its temperature exposure.
entries.animalRule: Change the location rather than adding powered cooling.
entries.userBenefit: You learn whether moving the setup solves discomfort more cheaply than fighting the environment.
entries.mechanismConnection: Black Sea Bass — Tracks bottom temperature closely both seasonally and across years, which has moved the population's centre of distribution several hundred kilometres north and made the fish common in waters where it was historically scarce. The Trial compresses that mechanism into one immediate, proofable human session.

entries.title: Move One Valuable Item Through Three Refuges
entries.objective: Move One Valuable Item Through Three Refuges.
entries.animalRule: You must stop at all three refuges; a direct run between any two of them ends the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: You practise mobility-based protection: when you cannot seal up, route choice becomes the defence.
